notes: Current registered control. Absence of a distinct pollinating anther is source-secure and the 2021 plastome tree places M. australasica sister to the sampled remainder of Monochoria. Direct species-level pollination evidence and exclusion of unsampled/alternatively sampled nonheterantherous congeners remain open.

Historical and comparative sources describe M. cyanea as lacking the case-defining stamen dimorphism or having equal stamens. It is included in older/2018 phylogenetic sampling but absent from the 2021 plastome sample used for the incumbent control. It must therefore be explicitly ruled in or out rather than ignored.
Current registered shared control. Heteranthery absence is source-secure; direct species-level pollination evidence and closest-eligible closure remain open.
Alternative non-dimorphic congener that must be included in the closest-control search. Current evidence is insufficient for promotion.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Luo et al. 2009 code long and short stamen sets and include S. surattensis among heteromorphic-stamen species.

A recent comparative synthesis labels S. rugosa non-heterantherous and cites Braga et al. 2022, but primary-source confirmation of the absence criterion, direct pollinator eligibility and the closest-control phylogenetic comparison are not yet frozen.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Weaker differentiation than the case does not establish heteranthery absence.
Candidate only. S. rugosa may provide a genuinely nonheterantherous Senna comparison, but all three eligibility gates remain to be closed prospectively.
